clue.text: Bow from the Parisian, one having hesitation in farewell

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the'

indicators.note: the one-and-hesitation group is placed in the word for farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
the Roman numeral for one
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A French bow at someone's departure, made by a person who hesitates while saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' just joins one to hesitation, making IER, which goes in VALE after its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavalière is a loosely tied bow-style necktie, named after a French duchess.

clue.text: An order that is given creating hopelessness

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: An instruction is issued that leaves people in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given creating' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomie is social or personal alienation, a loss of purpose and hope.

clue.text: Used e.g. a restaurant that could provide tea

parts.note: read as wordplay, ATE with OUT as an anagram signal would rearrange into the drink named last

explanation.surface: Someone made use of a restaurant that could serve afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: OUT would signal an anagram of ATE, which gives TEA. 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine away from home means patronising a restaurant, using it for a meal.

clue.text: Killer represented in cinema

indicators.note: represented says the letters of cinema are presented afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A murderer as portrayed in films.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang an iceman is a professional hitman, a cold-blooded murderer.

clue.text: Do clergy ever start to exercise or possibly dance?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged otherwise
start to says the opening letter of exercise is used

explanation.surface: A wry question: do clergymen ever take up exercise, or perhaps a dance?
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Roger de Coverley is an English country dance, often the last at a ball.

clue.text: Graduate dumps case outside a library briefly

indicators.note: outside puts the case around the other pieces

parts.note: a crate is a packing case
lib is the short form of library

explanation.surface: A university graduate dumps a box outside a library for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: To graduate a gauge is to mark it with a scale, which is to set its markings precisely.

clue.text: In chorus, in The Good Old Days?

explanation.surface: Singing together, as audiences did at The Good Old Days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Old Days was a long-running BBC television music-hall show where the audience sang along.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both simultaneously and formerly, once upon a time.

clue.text: The old man has to run around building that may be coming down

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: around says the run word goes about the building

parts.note: to race is to run
a hut is a small building

explanation.surface: Father has to run round a building that may be about to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A parachute is a canopy device that is in use while it descends through the air.

clue.text: Sacred text from a part of Scripture fed to backsliding member

indicators.note: the A and NT go into the reversed limb like food into a mouth
sliding back says the limb word is read from the end

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A sacred text drawn from Scripture is given to a church member who has lapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' sounds like a lapsed churchgoer, but it only turns the limb word round; 'fed to' puts the rest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred verbal formula or text repeated in Hindu and Buddhist prayer.

clue.text: One rules, i.e. governs somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters can be worked into a new order

parts.note: the abbreviation gives its two letters

explanation.surface: A statement that one person rules, that is, governs in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges IE plus GOVERNS. The definition reads as 'one [who] rules'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a monarch, a person who reigns over a state.

clue.text: Brownish drug I injected

indicators.note: injected says the letter I goes inside the drug word, like a needle

parts.note: senna is a plant-based laxative drug

explanation.surface: A brownish drug into which the speaker has injected something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment of yellowish or reddish brown, so the colour is brownish.

clue.text: Images created by artist at the end of new musical

indicators.note: at the end of puts the artist after the rearranged letters
new says the word musical is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Pictures produced by a painter at the close of a newly staged musical show.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulacra are images or likenesses, especially superficial representations of something.

clue.text: Miserable fellow and wife facing strain

parts.note: to retch is to strain as if vomiting

explanation.surface: An unhappy man whose wife puts him under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unfortunate or unhappy person, a poor soul.

clue.text: Aim to be dispassionate

definitions.meaning: free of personal feeling or bias

explanation.surface: The goal is to remain unemotional.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a goal; as an adjective it means impartial.

clue.text: Woman taking men round a French church is one to be listened to

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: round says the soldiers go about the French article and church

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
un is French for a
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman takes some men around a church in France, and they must heed her.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who reads the news or introduces programmes speaks for an audience to hear.

clue.text: Board to board?

parts.note: a plank of wood used for getting on a ship

explanation.surface: A puzzling phrase about a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is a movable plank for walking onto or off a vessel, hence a plank for embarking.

clue.text: Regular characters in these taverns

indicators.note: in says the letters are found lying within these two words

explanation.surface: The regular customers to be found in these pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular characters' suggests alternate letters; the run sits across 'these taverns' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a group of people who regularly mix together, a circle of regulars.

clue.text: The ship to drop with 500 lost

indicators.note: lost says the numeral is removed

parts.note: to shed is to drop or cast off
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: The ship drops five hundred, which are lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are traditionally referred to with the feminine pronoun.

clue.text: Top of the leg showing? It's the fashion

indicators.note: top of, in a down clue, takes the opening letter of the

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A short skirt shows the top of the leg, and that is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing?' is a link. The leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The ton is an old term for the prevailing fashion or fashionable society.

clue.text: It's here you may find dictionary's content despicable

definitions.text: It's here you may find dictionary's content
definitions.meaning: in alphabetical order the headword content comes just after, below, contempt

explanation.surface: A despicable dictionary, or one with despicable contents.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the entry 'content' is found below 'contempt' in any dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so bad it does not even merit scorn is utterly despicable; the phrase is an idiom for that.

clue.text: A long time in school, not a short time

indicators.note: not says the time letter is left out of the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A long stretch spent at school, as opposed to a brief one.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long period, an age.

clue.text: A single revolutionary that disgusts me — I want no more!

indicators.note: revolutionary means the number word turns around

parts.note: a single is one
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone sick of a lone revolutionary who disgusts them declares they've had their fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you have had sufficient is the exclamation of someone who wants nothing further.

clue.text: Alloy partially hollowed out on top of aged stones

indicators.note: in a down clue the alloy part goes above the age
one of the two middle letters of the alloy is removed, emptying it partly

parts.note: steel is an alloy of iron
one of the pair of middle letters of the alloy word, the one scooped out
ae abbreviates Latin aetatis, aged

explanation.surface: A metal partly scooped out sits on top of ancient stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Stelae are upright stone slabs bearing inscriptions or carvings.

clue.text: Part of Ukraine, area with cold and frost to the north of it

indicators.note: in a down clue cold and frost sit above the area

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A part of Ukraine with cold weather and frost to its north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula on the Black Sea is internationally recognised as Ukrainian territory.

clue.text: Saintly woman's nickname, as some posh types might say?

indicators.text: as some posh types might say
indicators.note: a plummy drawl drops the final r, so the name word comes out sounding like a girl's name

parts.note: a moniker is a name or nickname

explanation.surface: The pet name of a holy woman, as pronounced by the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: St Monica was the mother of St Augustine of Hippo.

clue.text: Man of 18?

parts.note: 18 down is a ton, a hundred; a Roman officer commanded a hundred men

explanation.surface: An eighteen-year-old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is not an age but the answer to 18 down, TON, slang for a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman centurion led a century, a unit of a hundred soldiers.

clue.text: Get ensnarled in seaweed

definitions.meaning: to become caught up or knotted
a large brown kelp of the genus Laminaria

explanation.surface: To get caught up in seaweed while swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means become twisted or caught up, and the noun is a name for oarweed kelp.

clue.text: After drink's knocked back one gets weak during battle

indicators.note: knocked back says the drink word is read in reverse, with a pun on drinking it

parts.note: ale is beer
lame means weak or feeble
in means during

explanation.surface: After downing a drink, a man feels feeble in the middle of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns ALE into ELA; 'one gets' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of the decisive Second World War battle of 1942.

clue.text: Girl of 15 suffers setback after earlier struggle in the capital

parts.note: to vie is to contend or struggle

indicators.note: a setback sends the name backwards

parts.note: Ann is the woman's name used in 15 down

explanation.surface: A fifteen-year-old girl has a setback after an earlier struggle while in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of 15' is not an age: it points to the woman's name at the start of the wordplay for 15 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Man in wicked guise first to relish a naughty foreign city

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil form of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's tale

indicators.note: first to says only the opening letter of relish is wanted

parts.note: bad means naughty

explanation.surface: A man disguised as a villain is the first to enjoy a wicked city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyderabad is a large city in India, and another in Pakistan.
